about: Mutants no test can kill because they do not change behaviour (equivalent mutants). Each is listed with the label symbolics.mutate prints, and with the reason it is equivalent, so a reader can disagree with the reason. A label names a line number: if the code moves, the label stops matching and the mutant is reported as a survivor again, which is the safe direction. Recorded 2026-11-20.

why.symbolics/family_f.py:200 (Or->And): In matching_rules(), `not nx or not ny` becomes `and`. Recorded 2026-11-22. When only one side of a study pair is empty, the mutant goes on instead of returning [] at once, but it still returns []: no rule applies to empty text (apply gives None, never equal to a word), and no rule turns a word into empty text (it gives None or a word, never ''). So no rule is consistent with that pair either way.
why.reference_agent/mcp.py:148 (Gt->GtE): time.monotonic() > deadline becomes >=. They differ only at the single instant the clock equals the deadline, which no test can hit on purpose and which changes nothing but whether one more line is read.
why.athanor/codec.py:12 (Lt->LtE): e < 2 becomes e <= 2. At e = 2 both branches give the same bits: 0x00200000 << 2 = 0x00800000, and (2 - 1) << 23 = 0x00800000.
why.athanor/codec.py:63 (Lt->LtE): factor < 0 becomes factor <= 0. factor == 0 returned earlier (codec.py:58), so this line never sees 0.
why.athanor/codec.py:63 (Gt->GtE): abs(k - round(k)) > 1e-12 becomes >= 1e-12. They differ only if log2 of a float lands exactly 1e-12 from an integer, which no real factor does.
why.athanor/gguf.py:55 (NotEq->Eq): et != 7 only keeps bool arrays off the fast path. The slow path reads the same values one at a time with the same struct format, so the result is the same either way.
why.athanor/workshop.py:53 (Eq->NotEq): (Was line 21 before the lock retry was added above it.) On Windows, os.name == 'nt' becomes != and the move uses os.replace instead of MoveFileExW with write-through. Both replace the file atomically; they differ only in durability across a power loss, which no test can observe. On Linux the mutant calls kernel32 and fails, so it is killed there (CI).
